title: Designing an AI-Assisted Workflow for a Real-World Problem
introduction: In this lesson you will learn how to turn a real problem into a step‑by‑step AI workflow. By the end you can choose the right AI tools, write effective prompts, and check the results for usefulness and safety.

sections.heading: Understanding the Problem
sections.subheading: Define the goal and scope clearly
paragraphs: Start by writing down what you want to achieve. A clear goal helps you pick the right AI actions.
Identify any constraints such as time, budget, or data availability. This keeps the workflow realistic.

example.title: Example: Improving a Study Schedule
example.content: A high‑school student wants a weekly study plan that balances math, science, and language practice while leaving time for hobbies.

sections.heading: Choosing the Right AI Tools
sections.subheading: Match each task with an appropriate AI capability
paragraphs: Look at the list of AI abilities you have learned: text generation, summarisation, image creation, data analysis, etc. Choose the one that fits each sub‑task.
Consider cost, speed, and accuracy. For a simple text summary, a free language model may be enough, while data analysis might need a specialised tool.

example.title: Example: Using a Language Model for Summaries
example.content: To create a short summary of a long article, the learner selects a text‑summarisation model and writes a prompt asking for a 3‑sentence overview.

sections.heading: Creating Prompt Sequences
sections.subheading: Break the workflow into small, ordered steps
paragraphs: Write each step as a separate prompt. This makes it easier to test and improve each part.
Use clear instructions and give examples in the prompt so the AI knows the expected format.

example.title: Example: Step‑by‑Step Prompt Chain
example.content: Step 1: Ask the AI to list key topics from the article. Step 2: Prompt it to write a brief explanation for each topic. Step 3: Request a final summary that combines the explanations.

sections.heading: Testing and Evaluating Results
paragraphs: Run the prompts and review the output. Look for missing information, errors, or unclear language.
If the result is not satisfactory, adjust the prompt wording or add more context, then test again.

example.title: Example: Reviewing Generated Study Plan
example.content: The student checks the AI‑created schedule for balanced subject time, realistic study hours, and inclusion of breaks. Any gaps are corrected by refining the prompts.

sections.heading: Managing Risks and Human Oversight
sections.subheading: Identify where human verification is needed
paragraphs: AI can make mistakes or produce biased content. Decide which steps require a human to double‑check the output.
Document the verification points so you can consistently apply the same safety checks each time you use the workflow.

example.title: Example: Verifying Financial Advice
example.content: When using AI to suggest a small business budget, the owner reviews each expense suggestion against actual invoices before finalising the plan.

practice.title: Build a Mini AI Workflow
practice.instruction: Choose a simple everyday problem (e.g., planning a grocery list). Write two short prompts: one to gather needed items and another to organise them by store sections. Run the prompts and note if the list meets your needs.

keyTakeaways: Clear problem definition guides the whole AI workflow.
Select AI tools that match each specific sub‑task for better results.
Break the process into small prompts, test, and refine each step.

mcqs.question: What is the first step when designing an AI‑assisted workflow for a real‑world problem?
options: Define the goal and scope clearly
Choose the AI model to use
Write the code for the workflow
Deploy the solution to production
mcqs.explanation: The lesson states that you should start by writing down what you want to achieve; a clear goal guides tool selection and later steps.

mcqs.question: Which factor is most important when selecting an AI tool for a sub‑task?
options: The color of the user interface
Cost, speed, and accuracy of the tool
The number of users who have tried it
The brand popularity of the provider
mcqs.explanation: The lesson advises considering cost, speed, and accuracy to match the tool to the specific sub‑task.

mcqs.question: In a prompt chain, why is it recommended to give examples in each prompt?
options: To make the prompts longer and more detailed
To help the AI understand the expected format
To reduce the number of tokens used
To hide the real task from the AI
mcqs.explanation: Providing examples shows the AI the desired output style, making the response more reliable.

mcqs.question: During testing, a student finds that the AI‑generated study schedule lacks breaks. What is the best next action?
options: Accept the schedule as it is
Adjust the prompt to request breaks and retest
Delete the AI output and create the schedule manually
Increase the model temperature to get more varied output
mcqs.explanation: The lesson recommends refining the prompt wording or adding more context when the result is unsatisfactory.

mcqs.question: Which step most likely requires human verification according to the lesson?
options: Generating a list of grocery items
Summarising an article
Verifying financial advice suggestions
Formatting the final report
mcqs.explanation: The lesson’s risk‑management section highlights that steps like financial advice need a human to double‑check the AI output.
